claims.text: An aggregate root is the one entity of an aggregate that outside code holds and calls; every change inside the aggregate goes through the root's methods (Evans' DDD, Aggregates).

claims.text: At stage-3 Order keeps items in `private readonly List<OrderItem> items = [];` and exposes `public IReadOnlyList<OrderItem> Items => items.AsReadOnly();`; the ctor first runs `this.items.AddRange(items);`, then checks the copy. No other Order member adds, removes or changes an item.

claims.text: IReadOnlyList<T> declares no Add, Remove or Clear, so `order.Items.Clear()` and `order.Items.Add(...)` fail to compile; at stage-3 `order.Items[0].Quantity = 0` fails to compile because the setter is private (inaccessible set accessor).
claims.source_hint: .NET API: IReadOnlyList<T>, IReadOnlyCollection<T> members; C# docs: Access modifiers on accessors (restricting accessor accessibility)

claims.text: List<T>.AsReadOnly() returns a ReadOnlyCollection<T> wrapping the list; calling Clear/Add/Remove through its IList<T> interface throws NotSupportedException. Test Items_CannotBeChangedFromOutside asserts this.
claims.source_hint: .NET API: List<T>.AsReadOnly, ReadOnlyCollection<T> (explicit IList<T>.Clear throws NotSupportedException); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Tests/Domain/OrderTests.cs:135-144

claims.text: List<T>.AddRange copies the elements (references) into the target list; clearing the source list, or adding to it, afterwards leaves the target unchanged, while the item objects themselves are shared. Test Constructor_CallerClearsItsList_OrderKeepsItsItems asserts the clearing case.
At stage-3 OrderItem is `public sealed class OrderItem(int productId, int quantity, Vnd unitPrice)` with OrderId, ProductId, Quantity and UnitPrice all `{ get; private set; }`.
A readonly field can be assigned only in its declaration or a constructor of its class; afterwards the list object cannot be replaced, though its contents can still be changed by code that holds it.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: readonly keyword (readonly field)

claims.text: `e.Navigation(o => o.Items).HasField("items").UsePropertyAccessMode(PropertyAccessMode.Field)` makes EF Core read and write the backing field `items` instead of the Items property, both when materializing (loading) and when saving.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Backing Fields (Configuring backing fields; Field and property access, PropertyAccessMode.Field); NavigationBuilder.HasField

claims.text: At stage-3 IOrderRepository has FindAsync, ListByCustomerAsync, AddAsync, SaveChangesAsync, FindForReadingAsync, FindByIdempotencyKeyAsync; none takes or returns an OrderItem. EfOrderRepository.FindAsync is `db.Orders.Include(o => o.Items)...`, loading all of the order's items.

At stage-3 OrderService creates OrderItem objects only to pass them to a new Order (OrderService.cs:37) and otherwise loads orders with repository.FindAsync, calls Cancel()/Ship() on them, then repository.SaveChangesAsync().

When the root checks a part's rules, giving the part (OrderItem) its own repository is a mistake: code could change it without the root; a change to an item (support's request) belongs in a new Order method. Opposing context: a thing others must find and change alone is a separate aggregate.
claims.source_hint: outline misconception 2; Evans' DDD, Repositories (one per aggregate root)
